dragon_guide.text: Dragon Hall was built around 1430 by a rich merchant, Robert Toppes, as a grand showroom for his cloth and goods, right on the river so the boats could unload at the back door.
Look up at the crown-post roof. In the corner there's a carved, painted dragon. For centuries the hall was split into houses and shops, and nobody remembered it was there until the 1980s.
Norwich was one of the richest cities in England then, on wool and worsted cloth. Worsted is named after Worstead, a Norfolk village. Your jumper might be Norfolk-born.
